headline_findings: There are no weights. A drop table is a flat 16-byte row of item ids; P(item) = count/16, one uniform roll. 0xFF = no drop. Both tables live in disc blobs, not in the decomp - they are transcribed here.

Every shop price was recovered. The decomp has almost none of them (they are BMG INF1 fields), but the already-ripped message table does, and each price is printed next to the message text that states it.

The chart -> sea-sector -> reward table is recovered from placement data. The decomp has no such table; this file has all 49 rows, and the chart numbers independently match getCollectMapNum's odd 1..51-minus-35-and-36 set.
12 + 44 + 24 = 80 = the max-life clamp. Six bosses drop a Heart Container and there are 44 Pieces of Heart; the arithmetic closes exactly, which is how the world totals are pinned without a table.
No-drop is the most common outcome everywhere: 0x3F is the single most frequent itemNo on pots, grass and rocks alike.

_drops._headline: There is no weight column anywhere in Wind Waker. A drop table is a FLAT 16-BYTE ROW of item ids; the probability of item X is simply (how many of the 16 slots hold X) / 16, picked by one uniform cM_rndF(15.9999f). Slot value 0xFF means NO DROP. That is the whole mechanism, for pots, grass, rocks and enemies alike.
_drops._names_that_do_not_exist: For the record, so nobody hunts for them again: fopAcM_createDropItem, fopAcM_createItemForMidBoss, l_dropItemTbl, l_itemTable, dProbability and itemProb DO NOT EXIST in this codebase - a repo-wide grep returns zero hits. Those are Twilight Princess / Ocarina names. cLib_getRndValue is never used in drop code either; drop RNG is exclusively cM_rndF / cM_rndFX (src/SSystem/SComponent/c_math.cpp:185). Also note d_a_itembase.cpp contains NO table - it is only the base draw/anim class; the per-item data lives in src/d/d_item_data.cpp.

fopAcM_createItemFromTable.role: THE object drop roll - pots, grass, rocks, crates, switch-items.
fopAcM_createItemFromTable.param: i_tableNo is 6 bits (JUT_ASSERT < 64 at :807). 0x00-0x1F = a literal dItemNo, spawned with no roll. 0x20-0x3E = tableIdx = param - 0x20, an index into ItemTableList::mItemTables[0x1E][0x10]. 0x3F (and 0xFF) = spawn nothing (:893-894).

fopAcM_createItem.role: spawn one exact item id, no table indirection
fopAcM_createItem.special_cases: dItemNo_RECOVER_FAIRY_e spawns fpcNm_NPC_FA1_e instead; dItemNo_TRIPLE_HEART_e creates two extra hearts then falls through for the third (:986-997)

fopAcM_createItemForTrBoxDemo.role: what a treasure chest calls when it opens
fopAcM_createItemForTrBoxDemo.param: full 8-bit itemNo, JUT_ASSERT 0 <= itemNo < 256. NO table indirection - a chest always holds exactly the item its rot.z high byte names. Calls dComIfGp_event_setGtItm(itemNo) first so the get-item cutscene knows what to show, and bails on 0xFF.

fopAcM_createItemForPresentDemo.role: NPC hand-over. Same as TrBoxDemo but forwards a caller-supplied argFlag into bits 16-23 of the demo-item params (:952).

fopAcM_createItemForBoss.role: hard-wired to dItemNo_HEART_CONTAINER_e with itemBitNo = -1 and type = daItemType_3_e. The second argument is genuinely unused. param_6 == 1 selects daItemAct_BOSS_e, anything else daItemAct_BOSS_DISAPPEAR_e.

fopAcM_createDisappear.role: what a DYING ENEMY actually calls. Packs (itemBitNo & 0xFF) << 16 | (scale & 0xFF) << 8 | dropType, and critically copies actor->itemTableIdx onto the Disappear actor (:1306) so the enemy's drop row survives its own deletion.

fopAcM_createIball.role: the enemy-death coin flip: life ball (8 items at once) vs one item from the enemy table

fopAcM_createItemFromEnemyTable.role: uniform 1-of-16 roll over the enemy row N_ITEM0..15, with de-dup filtering, then getItemNoByLife, then spawn with speedF = cM_rndFX(5.0f), speedY = 50 + cM_rndFX(10), gravity = -6.0

object_drop_table._how_to_use: A placed object stores a 6-bit itemNo. Below 0x20 it is a literal item id. From 0x20 to 0x3E it selects row (value - 0x20) of this table. 0x3F means no drop.
object_drop_table._health_scaling: Rows 0x01-0x04 are special: if an object asks for any of them, the request is OVERWRITTEN by Link's health bracket before the roll (src/f_op/f_op_actor_mng.cpp:821-843). lifePercent = 100 * life / (maxLife & 0xFC); 81-100% -> row 1, 41-80% -> row 2, 21-40% -> row 3, 1-20% -> row 4, exactly 0% -> unchanged. THIS IS THE ENTIRE "hearts when you are low" MECHANISM - it swaps the whole table rather than special-casing hearts. The & 0xFC means loose heart pieces do not count toward max health here.
object_drop_table._off_by_one_bug: mEntryCount is 30, so valid rows are 0..0x1D, but the code accepts a param up to 0x3E which yields tableIdx 0x1E - one row past the array, reading the 16 trailing zero bytes of the file. Zero is dItemNo_HEART_e, so param 0x3E behaves as "always a heart" by accident. Reproduce it if you want parity. confidence: high.

_how_an_enemy_death_resolves: 1. The enemy calls fopAcM_createDisappear(actor, pos, scale, dropType, itemBitNo) and its itemTableIdx is copied onto the Disappear actor (src/f_op/f_op_actor_mng.cpp:1306).

2. The Disappear actor waits 58 frames (src/d/actor/d_a_disappear.cpp:70, mTimer = 58 + REG8_S(0)) then dispatches on dropType (:19-53): 1 or 3 = NO DROP; 2 = fopAcM_createItemForBoss (heart container); 10/11/12 = a fixed {HEART, LARGE_MAGIC, ARROW_10} lookup, 13 is out of range and drops nothing; anything else (0 = IBALL) = the normal path.

3. fopAcM_createIball rolls the LIFE BALL: dropChance = the enemy's 'percent' column, randPercent = cM_rndF(99.999f). If dropChance > randPercent, spawn a life ball; otherwise call fopAcM_createItemFromEnemyTable for a single item (src/f_op/f_op_actor_mng.cpp:1234-1263).

4a. A life ball is NOT a roll - daIball_c deterministically bursts ALL EIGHT ITEM0..ITEM7 columns with randomised angles and speeds (src/d/actor/d_a_ib.cpp:115-169). Its items live only 90 + 60 frames (:109).
4b. A single drop is one uniform cM_rndF(15.999f) over N_ITEM0..15, then de-dup filtering, then getItemNoByLife (src/f_op/f_op_actor_mng.cpp:1179-1232).
enemy_drop_table._reading_the_percent_column: 'percent' is the chance out of 100 of dropping a LIFE BALL (8 items at once) INSTEAD of one item from N_ITEM. Moblin, Darknut, Stalfos, Armos, Ghost Ship, wiz_m and Morth sit at 100 and therefore always burst. Bokoblin, Keese and most ChuChus sit at 5. Blue ChuChu and Miniblin sit at 0 with an all-0xFF N_ITEM row, so they drop nothing on this path at all - Blue Chu Jelly comes through the grapple-steal path, Miniblin through the Ganon's Tower special case below.

no_drop_and_anti_farm._headline: There is NO global 'recently dropped' counter and NO farm timer anywhere - I looked for one. Instead the game uses seven separate mechanisms.

mechanisms.detail: the primary no-drop weight. Row 0x0A is 87.5% nothing; rows 0x1C and 0x1D are 93.75% nothing.

post_roll_substitutions.check_itemno: Substitutes GREEN_RUPEE when you cannot use the item: no magic meter -> magic jars (:2882); no bow -> arrows (:2888-2894); no bomb bag -> bombs (:2896-2901); no Bait Bag -> bait (:2902-2906); no Spoils Bag -> spoils (:2907-2911). Also TRIPLE_HEART -> HEART (:2912). src/d/d_item.cpp:2881-2916.

THE_ARITHMETIC_THAT_PINS_THE_WORLD_TOTAL._what: No table in the game states how many Pieces of Heart or Heart Containers exist - the collectibles pass confirmed that explicitly. But the numbers are forced, and this is the single cleanest result in this file:
THE_ARITHMETIC_THAT_PINS_THE_WORLD_TOTAL.containers_evidence: the census found exactly six Bitem (fpcNm_BOSSITEM_e) placements naming distinct save stages 2,3,4,5,6,7 = STAGE_FF, DRC, FW, TOTG, ET, WT (include/d/d_save.h:882-887). THE_ARITHMETIC_THAT_PINS_THE_WORLD_TOTAL.conclusion: the game contains 6 Heart Containers and 44 Pieces of Heart, and collecting all of them lands you on exactly 20 hearts with nothing wasted. confidence: high - the arithmetic is exact and the container count is independently confirmed by placement data.

_hearts.persistence_of_a_loose_piece: src/d/actor/d_a_item.cpp:768 calls fopAcM_onItemForIb(mItemBitNo, itemNo, roomNo) -> dComIfGs_onItem(bitNo, roomNo) (include/f_op/f_op_actor_mng.h:396-404). mItemBitNo is masked to 7 bits and 0x7F means "never remember" (src/d/actor/d_a_item.cpp:226-232). Storage is dSv_memBit_c::mItem, a SINGLE u32 = 32 bits per save-stage slot (include/d/d_save.h:679), so item bits are per-stage-group and not per-room. A heart piece in a CHEST uses the chest's tboxNo bit instead.

_census._what: Everything here was COUNTED, not read from the decomp. Source: Z:/3d ripper/out/rip/GZLE01/godot/stage_data.json - 161 stages, 19738 actor placements, 702 distinct actor names. IMPORTANT PARSING NOTE: the rip splits each stage's placement list into THREE buckets ('actors', 'tags', 'logic'); a census that reads only 'actors' misses grass, salvage points and much else. All three are scanned below. Chunk mix: ACTR 9032, TGOB 311, TGDR 307, TRES 237, SCOB 223, DOOR 16.

_excluded_stages.note: Only these are dropped from the 'shipping' figures. DEV/TEST are debug maps (K_Test*, I_Test*, ITest6*, TEST, VrTest, H_test, E3ROOP), the file-select and title-demo maps (Name, DmSpot0), and two empty stubs (Mukao, Ebesso have zero placements). DUPLICATE_ROOM_VARIANTS are alternate single-room copies of a stage that also exists in full (sea_r11/sea_r44 duplicate sea rooms 11 and 44; LinkRM_r44 and M_NewD2_r44 likewise). SUSPECT: Cave08 holds 11 chests whose contents are a near-exact copy of the Wind Temple 'kaze' (both give charts 13 and 23, three Joy Pendants, a Boss Key, a Map, a Compass) - it looks like an abandoned duplicate. Excluding it is a JUDGEMENT CALL, not something the code states; add 11 chests back if you disagree. confidence: medium. Cutscene-only and interior stages (Ocmera, morocam, Msmoke, Nitiyou, MajyuE, kenroom, Adanmae, Abesso, the A_*/​*umi movie stages) are deliberately KEPT - they are retail content.

chests._decode: Confirmed against source, not assumed: itemNo = home.angle.z >> 8 & 0xFF (include/d/actor/d_a_tbox.h:37); tboxNo = params >> 7 & 0x1F (:35); switch = params >> 12 & 0xFF (:36); funcType = params & 0x7F (src/d/actor/d_a_tbox.cpp:403-405); shapeType = (params >> 0x14) & 0x0F, forced to 0 when >= 4 (:397-401). The LOW byte of rot.z is a second switch, turned on when the chest is opened (src/d/actor/d_a_tbox.cpp:866-870).
chests._decode_cross_check: INDEPENDENT PROOF the bit layout is right. dSv_memBit_c::onTbox asserts 0 <= no < 32 and does mTbox |= 1 << no (src/d/d_save.cpp:1072-1075), so tboxNo must be unique inside one stage's save slot. Measured across the shipping stages that hold chests, tboxNo IS unique in every stage except two, and both exceptions are the SAME chest listed twice at byte-identical coordinates on different layers. A wrong shift would have produced collisions everywhere. confidence: high.
chests._distinct_note: 193 shipping placements collapse to 181 distinct chests. 3 are pure layer variants at identical coordinates; the rest are one physical chest duplicated across stage variants of one room - ma2room / ma3room / majroom are the three story-state copies of the Forsaken Fortress interior and PShip / PShip2 / PShip3 the three copies of the pirate ship, so their chests were merged. Both numbers are given; pick whichever your remake needs.

func_type_meanings.src: src/d/actor/d_a_tbox.cpp:23-31. Types 7 and 8 write their opened-bit into the STAGE_SEA2 save slot instead of the current stage (src/d/actor/d_a_tbox.cpp:857-863) - in the measured data these are exactly the island/sea chests that must survive sailing away.

chests.shape_type_note: 0 = BOXA (short), 1 = BOXB, 2 = BOXC, 3 = BOXD (l_modelInfo[4], src/d/actor/d_a_tbox.cpp:35-67). Values >= 4 found in the data are folded to 0 at runtime by getShapeType.

salvage._what: Salvage points are PLACED ACTORS ('Salvage' / 'SwSlvg'), not a table in the executable - there is no l_salvageTbl anywhere in src/. Decode from src/d/d_salvage.cpp:12-19: kind = params >> 28, svNo = params >> 20 & 0xFF, roomNo = params >> 12 & 0xFF, itemNo = params >> 4 & 0xFF, type = params & 0x0F, switchNo = home.angle.z & 0xFF, candidate index = home.angle.z & 0x03.

THE_CHART_TABLE._headline: This answers a question the decomp CANNOT: chart number -> which Great Sea sector to sail to -> what you actually get. The collectibles pass established that no chart->position table exists in code; this is that table, recovered from placement data. There are exactly 49 kind-0 salvage points in the 'sea' stage, one per sea room 1..49, each placed FOUR times (196 placements) at four candidate positions distinguished by home.angle.z & 3; the game shows only the set matching dSv_player_info_c::mRandomSalvagePoint, which a new file randomises to 0/1/2 (src/d/d_save.cpp:986-989) and which reinit() sets to 3 for the second quest (:1478).
THE_CHART_TABLE._cross_check: The chart numbers present are exactly 1..51 minus 35 and 36 - precisely the set dSv_player_map_c::getCollectMapNum() counts (src/d/d_save.cpp:918-927, which loops 1..61 skipping 35, 36 and everything >= 52). Two completely independent sources agreeing on the same odd 49-element set is strong evidence both the decode and the rip are correct. confidence: high.
THE_CHART_TABLE.triforce_charts_are_charts_1_to_8: Charts 1..8 are the Triforce Charts: their salvage points reward dItemNo_TRIFORCE1..8 (0x61..0x68), the Triforce SHARDS. Confirmed by src/d/actor/d_a_salvage.cpp:305-319, which hides a salvage point whose reward passes isTriforce() until dComIfGs_isCollectMapTriforce(itemNo - 0x60) is set - i.e. until Tingle has deciphered that chart.

salvage.kind2_note: 65 kind-2 points (64 in 'sea'). free_standing_items._what: Free-standing 'item' actors (fpcNm_ITEM_e): itemNo = params & 0xFF, itemBitNo = params >> 8 & 0xFF, spawn switch = params >> 16 & 0xFF, type = params >> 24 & 3, action = params >> 26 & 0x3F, collide switch = home.angle.z & 0xFF (include/d/actor/d_a_item.h:138-145).
free_standing_items._warning: Do NOT apply this decode to the other item-shaped actor names. 'Bitem' is fpcNm_BOSSITEM_e and its low byte is a dSv_save_c STAGE number, not an item id (include/d/actor/d_a_boss_item.h:12-14) - see boss_heart_containers below. 'Sitem' is worse: the name appears TWICE in the object-name table, once as fpcNm_SITEM_e (src/d/d_stage.cpp:920) and once as fpcNm_ShopItem_e (:1256), and src/d/actor/d_a_sitem.cpp is 100% empty /* Nonmatching */ bodies, so its params CANNOT be decoded from this decomp. The 38 'Sitem' placements (GanonD, kindan, K_Test5) are therefore left undecoded here rather than guessed.

hearts._note: The 44 kind-0 heart-piece PLACEMENTS are 11 charts x 4 candidate spots, so they are 11 heart pieces, not 44. The remaining pieces in the retail game are handed over by NPCs, minigames and events, which are not placed actors and therefore cannot be counted from stage data. See _hearts for the arithmetic that pins the world totals at 6 containers + 44 pieces.
hearts.boss_heart_containers_note: 'Bitem' = fpcNm_BOSSITEM_e. Its param low byte is a dSv_save_c STAGE index, and the actor only spawns the container if that stage's boss is dead and its LIFE bit is not yet set (src/d/actor/d_a_boss_item.cpp:28-35). The stage numbers found - 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 - are STAGE_FF, STAGE_DRC, STAGE_FW, STAGE_TOTG, STAGE_ET, STAGE_WT (include/d/d_save.h:882-887): exactly the six bosses that drop a Heart Container. Stage 2 (Forsaken Fortress) appears three times because the Helmaroc King container can be collected in M2tower or, if you left first, out on the sea (src/d/d_item.cpp:596-601).

breakables._headline: THE BIG NUMBER: 1932 pots/barrels/skulls, 3974 grass placements = 20902 cuttable blades, and 129 liftable rocks in shipping stages. itemNo 0x3F (NO DROP) is the single most common value in every one of the three tables - 25.1% of pots, 57.7% of grass, 19.4% of rocks. grass_literal_ids_seen_that_the_clamp_di.note: DISAGREEMENT WORTH KNOWING. d_a_grass.cpp:143-144 discards any grass itemNo below 0x20, yet the shipped placement data contains plenty of them - see grass_itemNo_field, where 0x00 (HEART), 0x01, 0x02, 0x09 and 0x0A together account for several hundred placements. Those placements do nothing at runtime. Either the level designers used a decode the runtime later stopped honouring, or these are intentional no-ops. A remake that honours the literal would hand out hundreds of free hearts the real game does not. confidence: high that the clamp exists and that the data contains sub-0x20 values; the reason is not in code.
